normalizeName('  Ada   Lovelace ');

# Job parsing and execution

Read this page before changing job input validation or the worker's handler interface. The workspace declaration is in [package.json](../package.json) and [pnpm-workspace.yaml](../pnpm-workspace.yaml).

## Ownership and flow

[Core's `parseJob`](../packages/core/src/index.js) parses JSON, requires a nonblank string `id`, and returns the original id with `payload`. It validates the trimmed id but does not trim the returned value. JSON parse errors propagate; the implementation does not provide a general object-schema validator.

[Worker's `runJob`](../packages/worker/src/index.js) calls the parser, passes only `payload` to the supplied handler, awaits its result, and returns `{ id, result }`. Parser exceptions and handler rejection propagate to the caller. There is no retry loop in this implementation. Core does not depend on the worker.

## Verification

[Worker tests](../test/worker.test.js) exercise payload delivery, preserved identity and handler failure. Run `node --test` at the workspace root. Changes to validation belong in core; changes to handler invocation and result wrapping belong in worker, with regression cases in the linked tests.

# Greeting service

A Node HTTP service returns JSON for health and greeting requests. Start it with `npm start` and run its unit tests with `npm test`, as defined in [package.json](package.json).

Before changing routes, environment configuration or container startup, read [service behavior and verification](docs/service.md). That page links the owning source, tests, CI and container configuration.

changes.content:
# Service behavior and verification

Use this page when changing request handling, startup configuration or the packaged container entrypoint.

## Request flow

[server.js](../src/server.js) reads configuration once at startup, creates an HTTP server, passes the parsed request URL to [handle](../src/handler.js), and writes its status and JSON body. The server sets `content-type: application/json`. Routing checks the URL pathname, not the HTTP method.

| Path | Response |
| --- | --- |
| `/health` | Status 200, `{ "ok": true }` |
| `/greet?name=Ada` | Status 200, `{ "message": "Hello, Ada" }` with the default prefix |
| Any other pathname | Status 404, `{ "error": "Not found" }` |

For `/greet`, an absent `name` parameter becomes `world`; an explicitly empty parameter stays empty. The configured prefix is followed by a comma and a space before the name.

## Configuration

[loadConfig](../src/config.js) converts `PORT` to a number and requires an integer between 1 and 65535. It defaults to 3000 when unset and throws `Invalid PORT` for invalid input. `GREETING_PREFIX` defaults to `Hello` when unset; an empty string is retained. Configuration errors occur before the server starts listening.

## Tests and packaging

[Service tests](../test/service.test.js) cover default configuration, an invalid port and a named greeting. [CI](../.github/workflows/test.yml) runs `npm test` with Node 22 on pushes and pull requests. The tests call configuration and handler functions directly; they do not prove live socket behavior.

The [Dockerfile](../Dockerfile) uses `node:22-alpine`, copies the manifest and source into `/app`, declares port 3000, and starts `node src/server.js`. A container port declaration does not override `PORT`. No production host, orchestration platform or release procedure is established by these files.

changes.content:
# Configuration

The default cache TTL is 5000 milliseconds, as defined by [createCache](../src/cache.js).

Pass a clock function as the second argument for deterministic tests.

## Expiration and clearing

Each cache instance owns an in-memory map. `getOrSet(key, make)` returns a stored value only while its deadline is strictly greater than the current clock. At the exact deadline it calls `make` again and stores a new deadline. [The boundary test](../test/cache.test.js) checks reuse at 4999 milliseconds and recomputation at 5000 milliseconds.

`clear()` removes all entries in that instance. If `make` throws, the call does not store a new entry. No background expiry timer or network persistence is implemented.
